entities.span: No schema change. This feature adds no table and no column, deliberately
rejected_spans: : acceptance is not recorded (see Consequences), and every fact the notice states is read from code and configuration that already exists.

entities.span: The AC-5 test asserts that the set of keys declared in `src/env.ts` is exactly the union of the two lists, with no key claimed twice and no entry naming a key that no longer exists.
rejected_spans: A stale entry fails just as loudly as an unclassified key, so the registry cannot quietly outlive the configuration it describes.

entities.span: The AC-23 test reads `src/lib/supabase/database.types.ts`, which is regenerated from the applied schema by `pnpm db:types`, and fails when a personal data table holds a column no entry names.
rejected_spans: This is the same guard as AC-5, pointed at the other half of the notice.

entities.span: It is not in the registry.
rejected_spans: The first draft of this criterion carried a `visibleToVisitor: false` entry for `src/features/demo/refresh-session.ts`, the demo refresh's own dedicated internal identity, on the theory that it "sets a cookie" internally but never for a visitor.

entities.span: **State transitions**: none. Both pages are static.
Neither page reads the session, reads the database, or opens a Sentry span.
rejected_spans: Binding rule 4 asks for a named span where a failure rate matters; a static prerender has no failure to rate, and opening one would add a client boundary these pages must not have.

entities.span: The recipient list on the page and the registry are the same list. The page never hardcodes a company name the registry does not hold.
rejected_spans: This is the shape that already failed once in this repo, where `hero-section.tsx` carried a written count beside a list that had moved on (`src/features/entry-page/AGENTS.md`).

entities.span: Every key in `src/env.ts` is accounted for by exactly one registry entry, or the suite fails. Most map to the recipient that receives them. Three reach no third party at all, two local switches and this site's own canonical address, and those are named in `ENV_KEYS_WITH_NO_RECIPIENT` with a reason each. Two of Vercel's three system values sit there too, because Vercel supplies them to the build rather than receiving them. The third, `NEXT_PUBLIC_VERCEL_ENV`, does not: Sentry stamps it on every event, so it is filed under Sentry. **What "reaches" means**: a key reaches a recipient when it is what connects this app to that company, its credential, its address, or a value transmitted to it. It reaches nobody only when no company is on the other end of it at all. A key supplied *by* a company is not thereby a key that reaches it, and if its value is sent onward to somebody else it belongs to that somebody. **Corrected on 2026-09-01, after the build.** This invariant first said every key maps to a RECIPIENT, which cannot be satisfied honestly. AC-5 itself is unchanged, and so is the forcing function.
rejected_spans: That mistake was made in this build and caught by a cross check, which is the case the definition below exists to prevent.
since features 11, 13 and 14 will each have to apply it
the only way to obey it literally is to file a local switch under a company, which would put a false sentence on a page whose entire value is that every claim on it can be checked

entities.span: Every column in a personal data table maps to exactly one field registry entry, or the suite fails.
rejected_spans: Invariants 1 and 2 protect the recipient list; this one protects the field list, and it exists because the cross check found the notice guarded on one side only.
entities.label: 2b

entities.span: Neither page may introduce `"use client"`.
rejected_spans: Both live under the marketing tree, whose `AGENTS.md` forbids it outright.

entities.span: The published address receives mail. Verified on 2026-09-01; verify checks it again rather than trusting the date.
rejected_spans: An address on a permanent public page that nobody reads is a silent failure, which this project's rules forbid.
it is the kind of thing that breaks later without telling anyone

entities.span: **Added 2026-09-18 (AC-24), revised the same day after a cross check.** The `Set-Cookie` names a real visitor's browser receives, driven through a real sign in, the real callback, and an ordinary signed in navigation, match the cookie registry exactly, or the suite fails. A secondary, cheaper unit test also maps every cookie setting call site under `src/` to a registry entry, but it is a known incomplete net, not the source of truth.
rejected_spans: This is the claim's real guarantee.
it would miss a wrapper function or a direct `Set-Cookie` header write, and it cannot by itself tell a real cookie store from something that merely resembles one in source text

entities.span: **Security model**: Both pages are public and hold no user data, so there is nothing to authorise. They read no session and query nothing.
these two routes deliberately opt back in to search indexing while every other route stays out, so the build must not widen that beyond the two pages.
**Configuration required**: No new environment variable.

Mail on `usejobhunt.dev` delivers `contact@usejobhunt.dev` to a mailbox that is read. **Already done**: configured and verified by the engineer on 2026-09-01, and corroborated here by DNS on the same day (Zoho MX at priorities 10, 20 and 50, plus an SPF record including `zohomail.com`).
rejected_spans: This is a prerequisite that is already met, not one the build waits on.

entities.span: Google Cloud console access, for AC-21 and AC-22.
Happy path: both pages render, and the recipient list on each matches the registry, verifies **AC-1**, **AC-3**, **AC-6**.
entities.label: Happy path

entities.span: Drift: adding a key to `src/env.ts` with no matching registry entry fails the unit suite, and removing the assertion is checked to fail the test, verifies **AC-5**.
rejected_spans: so it is not vacuous
entities.label: Drift

entities.span: Regression: changing a Sentry `dataCollection` value to send personal data fails a test, verifies **AC-4**.
rejected_spans: so the claim on the page cannot become false silently
entities.label: Regression

entities.span: Schema drift: adding a column to a personal data table without naming it in the field registry fails the unit suite, verifies **AC-23**.
entities.label: Schema drift

entities.span: Tracking drift: adding an analytics dependency or a third party script tag fails the unit suite, verifies **AC-14**.
entities.label: Tracking drift

entities.span: Cookie drift, real response (added 2026-09-18, revised after cross check): the integration suite drives sign in start, the callback, and an ordinary signed in navigation as three separate steps, and asserts each step's own `Set-Cookie` names against the registry, verifies **AC-24**.
rejected_spans: so a cookie added to what a visitor actually receives, at the step it actually appears, cannot quietly leave `/privacy` incomplete the way it already did once
entities.label: Cookie drift, real response (added 2026-09-18, revised after cross check)

entities.span: Cookie drift, source scan (secondary net): a new cookie setting call site under `src/` with no matching registry entry fails the unit suite, and a registry entry naming a call site that no longer exists also fails. A known non cookie in source text (an in memory jar, a deliberate no-op adapter) is explicitly excluded rather than silently matched, verifies **AC-24**.
rejected_spans: so the scan does not propose disclosing something that is not a cookie
entities.label: Cookie drift, source scan (secondary net)

entities.span: Metadata: the two pages are indexable while the root layout's robots assertions still pass, verifies **AC-17**.
entities.label: Metadata

entities.span: No client boundary: `/sign-in` still ships zero client JavaScript with the acceptance line added, verifies **AC-19**.
entities.label: No client boundary

entities.span: Delivery: a real message to the published address arrives, re confirmed at verify time rather than assumed from the setup date, verifies **AC-9**.
entities.label: Delivery
